name: Mage
summary: For a mage, arcane power answers to study, while the body remains frail beneath cloth armor. Fire, frost, and raw arcane force make mages formidable allies and dangerous foes. They conjure, teleport, and control the field of battle, but their discipline demands deep focus. Misused arcane power has left a perilous legacy.

sections.title: Scholars of the Arcane
sections.body: A mage’s path asks for intellect, focus, and years of study. Magi neither commune with spirits nor rely on divine faith; they approach magic as a precise cosmic science. Drawing on arcane energies, they unleash raw destruction, summon searing flame, or chill air into solid ice and howling blizzards. Heavy armor hinders the delicate gestures and concentration their incantations require, so they wear light cloth. Wards, mana barriers, and evasive spells help keep them safe.

sections.title: The Legacy of Dalaran and Arathor
sections.body:
Human magical tradition began nearly three millennia ago during the Troll Wars. High elven sorcerers taught one hundred humans of the Empire of Arathor to help turn the tide against the Amani. As more humans took up magic, citizens without such skill grew fearful, driving many magi to found the magocracy of Dalaran.

Governed by the Kirin Tor, Dalaran became the northern kingdoms’ central archive of magical study. There, combat magic took shape in traditions that served the Alliance of Lordaeron through the First and Second Wars.

sections.title: Suspicion and Necessity
sections.body:
Arcane practitioners have never won easy trust. The ancient cataclysm wrought by the Highborne and Dalaran’s fall during the Third War left many wary of magic’s volatile nature. The Church of the Holy Light has long viewed wizardry with suspicion.

Conservative knights have regarded arcane spellcasters as damned souls or a necessary evil in battle. Yet civil and military leaders know a capable magus can bring battlefield supremacy, swift mass transport, and vital defenses against supernatural threats.

sections.title: Mages of the Horde and the High Order
sections.body:
The arcane belongs to more than the Alliance. Troll and Forsaken mages serve the Horde, and orcs who study the art begin under Mai'ah, a Darkspear mage in the Valley of Trials. Mai'ah teaches that patience and careful judgment matter more than raw power.

Among the Skyborne, the High Order descends from the Highborne of Eldre'Thalas. Their time in Skywall cost them much of their ancestors’ arcane knowledge. With the wind spirits gone from Zephras Isle, they seek to recover it. Skyborne mages fight for the Alliance.

faq.q: What schools of magic do mages specialize in?
faq.answer: Mages study three core schools: Arcane, Fire, and Frost. Arcane alters time, space, and reality, allowing polymorphing, teleportation, and focused bursts of power. Fire brings swift, overwhelming combustion, while Frost slows, snares, and shatters foes before they can close to melee range.

faq.q: Why do mages only wear cloth armor?
faq.answer: Complex spells require free movement, precise hand gestures, and steady mental focus. Heavy materials such as leather, chainmail, or plate interfere with the gestures and concentration needed for incantations. Mages guard their physical vulnerability with magical barriers and spells that keep enemies at bay.

faq.q: How did humans first learn to cast arcane magic?
faq.answer: During the ancient Troll Wars, roughly two thousand eight hundred years ago, the human Empire of Arathor allied with the high elves of Quel'Thalas against the Amani trolls. In return for military aid, elven magi taught one hundred humans the fundamentals of arcane magic. These pioneers proved devastating in battle and began the human magical lineage that eventually founded Dalaran.

faq.q: What is the relationship between mages and the Church of the Holy Light?
faq.answer: The Church of the Holy Light and mages have a tense relationship. For centuries, orthodox members of the Church viewed arcane studies and the Kirin Tor with suspicion, sometimes treating them as heretical. Paladins and devout priests often see wizardry as unpredictable and morally dubious, though its strength in war makes it necessary.

faq.q: Are Stormwind's mages part of Dalaran's Kirin Tor?
faq.answer: Stormwind’s mages historically followed their own traditions, first led by court conjurers who worked largely apart from Dalaran. The Kirin Tor remained the northern center of magical learning, while southern wizards built their own enclaves and royal advisory roles. Communication and common ties between both realms endured.

faq.q: Can mages create food and transport people instantly?
faq.answer: Yes. Mages conjure fresh food and water from thin air, enchant allies’ intellects, and bend space to open portals that instantly connect major cities across the world.

Humans, gnomes, and the Skyborne train as Alliance mages; trolls, the Forsaken, and orcs serve as Horde mages. Dwarves, night elves, and tauren do not. Night elves shun the arcane after Queen Azshara’s Highborne brought ruin to ancient Kalimdor.

angles.text: As a mage, you need meticulous intellectual discipline. You master fire, frost, and arcane force while guarding the fragile balance of reality.
Your people’s arcane legacy reaches back to the hundred original magi taught during the Troll Wars. Their descendants built Dalaran into a great center of magical study.
As a night elf, you belong to a society that strictly shuns arcane magic, remembering the ruin Queen Azshara and her Highborne magi brought upon ancient Kalimdor.
As a paladin, you fight beside magi, though the Knights of the Silver Hand have long regarded their worldly arcane methods with deep caution.
As a warlock, you share a path many began as mages, before they abandoned academic restraint and strict Dalaran edicts to pursue demonic power.
As an orc mage, you begin your studies under Mai'ah, a Darkspear mage in the Valley of Trials. Mai'ah teaches patience and careful judgment before power.
As a Skyborne mage of the High Order, you seek to recover the Highborne spellcraft your ancestors carried out of Eldre'Thalas, hoping it can save your failing island.
